### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via canReadObject (literal, a string literal in callerMayReadObject))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via canReadObject (literal, a string literal in callerMayReadObject))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via canReadObject (literal, a string literal in callerMayReadObject))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e735b79ea52bfe41a04afd62e5490c60fbad757a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6f9ad22003ac11f3c7cc4819824d28f5b59410d4` — the merge of head `9fb84ac128d303c0e23da06e8376802ff02520cc` into base `e735b79ea52bfe41a04afd62e5490c60fbad757a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6f9ad22003ac11f3c7cc4819824d28f5b59410d4 && git checkout 6f9ad22003ac11f3c7cc4819824d28f5b59410d4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e735b79ea52bfe41a04afd62e5490c60fbad757a 9fb84ac128d303c0e23da06e8376802ff02520cc && git checkout -B drift-repro e735b79ea52bfe41a04afd62e5490c60fbad757a && git merge --no-ff 9fb84ac128d303c0e23da06e8376802ff02520cc

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e735b79ea52bfe41a04afd62e5490c60fbad757a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e735b79ea52bfe41a04afd62e5490c60fbad757a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9fb84ac128d303c0e23da06e8376802ff02520cc`
Local-runs: none
Scope: no `reviewFace` hits — the seven paths decide no face (no published schema, no governed path; the changeset reads `Clause-②: no`, not the narrowing arm), so this is the at-tier review ruling 5985885287 asks for before landing on the write-door existence boundary, served at the dispatched tier + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-batch-data.ts (`callerMayReadObject`, `runBatchDataLoop` cases `create` / `update` / `upsert`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (`runBatchDataLoop` host, `probeRecord`, `assertRecordExists`, `byIdUpdateRecord`, `searchAll`'s `canReadObject` note at :14806-14831), packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts (`canReadObject` :860-883), packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts (:263-268), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-object-admission.ts (`canReadObject`, `objectReadAdmission`), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts (step 2.7, :905-1157), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts (`callerCannotReadAddressedRow`, `absentUnderCallerRead`, `readUnlessRefused`), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-rls-filter.ts (:312-325), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (`createWithAutonumberResync` :8419-8500, the three `driver.create` sites), packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/memory-driver.ts (`create` :836, `markDirty` :2661), docs/adr/0120 (2026-11-01 amendment on `origin/main`), .changeset/batch-upsert-by-id-caller-read.md, the four test files of the diff.

Read-only shape held: the diff at this head (`git diff origin/main...FETCH_HEAD`), rulings 5985885287 (#21771) and 5934879010 (#21185), ADR-0120's amendment as merged by #28694, the sibling record 6561342764 on #28731, the head's check runs (68 runs: 57 success, 11 skipped, 0 failure), the PR's one comment (docs-drift). Nothing built or run. PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; `Implemented-by` is the branch.

### ① Derived judgments

The one changed body is the `case 'upsert'` fork of `runBatchDataLoop` for a row carrying an `id` (protocol-batch-data.ts :370-440). Before: `probeRecord` (system context) decided update-vs-insert on existence. Now: `callerMayReadObject` (object-level, once per loop, the security service's `canReadObject` with the loop's context) and then the caller's own `engine.findOne({ where: { id }, context })`; a truthy row takes the unchanged update arm, anything else takes the SAME `engine.insert` call and row builder as `case 'create'`. No fallback insert on either arm (kept). Judged per principal class, the question being whether any row can LAND at this head that could not before:

1. **read+edit, row visible to the caller** — `canReadObject` true, `findOne` returns the row, update arm, `engine.update` judges the write as before. Unchanged (dogfood `showcase_private_note` own row, walled B editor on B's row). **Correct.**
2. **read-only (read, no edit), row visible** — update arm, `engine.update`'s CRUD gate refuses `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, nothing lands. Unchanged (dogfood `showcase_task`, walled B creator on B's row; `showcase_account` control: one refusal for a held and an unknown id). **Correct.**
3. **read grant held, row hidden by RLS / sharing / the organization wall** — `findOne` returns `null` (hidden rows answer absence, not a throw: this is the same `value == null` the security layer's own `absentUnderCallerRead` reads as "cannot read"), insert arm, `engine.insert` collides on the primary key → `409 UNIQUE_VIOLATION`, the row's `errors` deep-equal to a batch create's for the same id (unit case 1; dogfood `showcase_inquiry`, `showcase_private_note` hidden, both walled personas on A's row, names neither A's id, name nor slug). Before: update arm → the pre-image check's `404` (or `403`) beside a `201` for an unknown id, i.e. the existence signal ruling 5985885287 closed on the other by-id doors. **Correct, and the intended change.** Nothing lands on a store that enforces the key.
4. **edit WITHOUT read** (`permission.zod.ts` :263-267 derives `allowRead` and `allowEdit` independently; only `modifyAllRecords` implies read) — `canReadObject` asks the `find` grant (`objectReadAdmission` step 5, `checkObjectPermission('find', …)`), so it answers `false` and EVERY row of the loop takes the insert arm without a row read (unit case 3). The insert arm never reads the edit bit: `engine.insert` judges `allowCreate`. So: without create → the create's `403`; with create (the create+edit-without-read class) → `409 UNIQUE_VIOLATION` on a PK-enforcing store. **Nothing lands at this head.** ⚠️ Before this diff, on this door, the class COULD land: the old fork sent the existing row to the update arm, and the security layer's step 2.7 (`security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts` :1146-1156) answers a by-id write whose read is REFUSED (a declared 4xx — the object's read grant withheld) by keeping today's admission when no write-class row filter binds (`computeRlsFilter` null: `security-plugin-rls-filter.ts` :312-325 derives the write class from the select class and leaves it empty when both are empty and the tenant wall does not apply) — the class record 6561342764 named on #28731 at the same seam. This diff CLOSES that path on the batch upsert door, because the update arm is now unreachable without a successful caller read. A removed landing, not an added one. Consequence for the PR text, under ③ and ⑤ below.
5. **create-only, no read** — `canReadObject` false → insert arm → `409` for a held id, `201` for an unknown one, as the plain create answers (dogfood creator persona). Before: update arm → `403`. Refusal to refusal. **Correct.**
6. **admins (`modifyAllRecords` / `viewAllRecords`), system context (`isSystem`)** — admission true (system bypass, or read implied by the bypass bit), `findOne` sees the row, update arm. Unchanged. **Correct.**
7. **context-less in-process call** (`context === undefined`) — not asked; `findOne` without a context, as its writes run. Unchanged (unit case 6). A `null` context is asked and the plugin answers `false` (principal-less, ADR-0096 D5) → insert arm, fail-closed. **Correct.**
8. **cross-organization, walled posture** — the wall hides A's row from B's reader, insert arm, the insert carries B's organization and collides on the deployment-global `id` → `409`, exactly ruling 5934879010 rule 2 extended by the 2026-11-01 amendment; the fresh id lands in B. **Correct** (dogfood walled suite, atomic and not).
9. **objects with write-class RLS** — a readable row the write policy refuses: update arm, step 2.7 refuses `403` as before. **Unchanged.**
10. **driver paths** — `engine.insert` reaches the store only through `driver.create` (engine.ts :8443, :8499, :16017); `driver.upsert` is never on this path, so no `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` can turn the insert arm into an overwrite. `createWithAutonumberResync` retries a unique violation only for a number the engine or driver issued; a caller-supplied `id` collision is enveloped on the first attempt (an object with an autonumber field whose driver does not name the colliding column re-issues the number and fails again on the same `id` — `ERR_AUTONUMBER_COLLISION`, nothing written; identical to `case 'create'`, pre-existing). `driver-memory`'s `create` pushes a second row with the same `id` (`assertUnique` enforces field-level `unique` only) — a DUPLICATE row for the classes in 3/4/5 above where the old fork answered a refusal. ADR-0120's amendment records exactly this for every create door ("not a production store, declares no primary key, so a duplicate `id` lands there"); flagged under ③ because `markDirty` can persist it through a `persistenceAdapter`.
11. **atomic arm** — the loop runs inside `runAtomicBatch` with the transaction's context, so both the admission and the row read ride the transaction (unit case 10: both `findOne` calls carry the handle), the causal row carries `UNIQUE_VIOLATION`, earlier rows `ROLLED_BACK`. **Correct.** Non-atomic with `continueOnError`: per-row, as before (unit case 11).
12. **`callerMayReadObject` semantics** — (a) a throwing `canReadObject` fails the row (and the batch, atomic): stricter than `ISecurityService.canReadObject`'s "callers must treat a throw as `false`" (security-service.ts :863-865) but fail-closed, the same stance `searchAll` took for the same method (protocol.ts :14826-14827); the shipped plugin never throws (it catches and answers `false`), and a throw gives the same answer for a held and an unknown id, so nothing is disclosed. Acceptable; noted under ③. (b) absent security service or a service predating the method → `true`, "not refused at this layer": the row read is still the middleware's, which refuses the object-level non-reader with `403` for every id — stricter than the create's answer, and the same for held and unknown ids. The contract text (:875-881) says compose the verdict from `explain` instead; `searchAll` already reasons as this fork does. No hole; noted under ③. (c) The once-per-loop cache is safe: one loop = one `object` and one `context` (a batch names one object; the atomic loop is one invocation under one transaction context), and a rejected promise is awaited on the same row that created it and re-awaited by later rows, so no unhandled rejection and every row answers alike.
13. **public face** — `BatchDataHost` (exported interface of a non-entry module) trades `probeRecord` for `getServicesRegistry`; `probeRecord`'s other readers (OCC) untouched; `protocol.ts`'s host object matches. No `packages/spec` change; no new error code (`UNIQUE_VIOLATION` is the registered one). The `findOne` options are typed `EngineQueryOptionsParsed` (no `as any`), and `check:query-options-erasure` reports none new.

Net: at this head no principal class can land a row it could not land before; one class (4) loses a landing the governing text never granted. Timing (a reader's extra `findOne` before the insert) is outside the ruling's shape and unchanged in kind from the old probe.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/metadata-protocol` **patch** — right. `Clause-②: no` is right: the accept set is not widened and no public face grows; the one movement is the removed landing in ① 4, which is a runtime security-behaviour change (execution-duties 负边界: not Clause-②) and, read as an accept-set narrowing, is still spelled `no` (execution-duties: 收窄已发布接受集的卡是 `Clause-②: no`, owing exactly this at-tier review). The `(narrowing)` arm is BREAKING and is for a declared capability taken away; ruling 5985885287 already governs that a row the caller cannot read does not exist on the write doors, so nothing declared is removed. `Metadata-protocol: none` — right, no authorable key moves. `Skills-docs: none` with reason — consistent with `git grep` of `skills/` as the body states. Changeset body matches the diff: readable row updated under the caller's write permissions, unreadable id takes the create arm and answers as a create naming it, id-less rows create, atomic rollback, system and context-less calls unchanged. One sentence to correct in the PR body (not the changeset): "A row it cannot read was never written by this door" is true of the ownership-floor domain and of every reader, and false for class ① 4 outside a write-class row filter — the body should say the arm is now unreachable for that class rather than that it never landed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; `Implemented-by` is the dev branch. Dev flags, each answered:
- **driver-memory duplicate** (body "Acceptance notes", fork comment) — acknowledged; the amendment rules it an accepted residual of every create door and this door now IS a create door for an unreadable id. Residual: with a `persistenceAdapter` (`markDirty`) the duplicate is persisted in a dev store. Not a must-fix (ruled); the docs-only follow-up below should say so.
- **ADR-0120 amendment's door list** — the amendment names the create doors (`POST /data/:object`, batch `create`, `createMany`, cross-object `/batch`, import `insert`/`upsert`, clone) and binds "⛔ No create door answers a collision on `id` differently by the visibility of the row that holds it". The batch `upsert` by-id fork is now such a door and is not listed. The seat's planned docs-only PR should add it (and note that this door, unlike import `upsert`, answers a held-but-unreadable id with the collision rather than a match). Should-fix, separate PR as planned.
- **Pin coverage, class ① 4 (edit without read, with and without create)** — no pin at this head: the dogfood personas hold read on every object they aim at except the create-only creator; the unit battery's object-refused case uses a context with no grants at all. The class the hardening closes is therefore unmeasured, and the ablation could not have gone red on it. **Not a must-fix for landing safety**: the update arm is structurally unreachable without a successful caller read (object admission asks the `find` grant; the insert arm never reads the edit bit), and the create-only persona measures the same code path. **Should-fix**: add an `allowRead: false, allowEdit: true` principal (±`allowCreate`) to the dogfood `HIDDEN` table on an object outside the ownership floor's domain, asserting the create's answer and the stored row untouched, so the one class this PR exists for is pinned by name.
- **Contract text vs. this fork** (① 12 a/b): `ISecurityService.canReadObject`'s docblock asks callers to treat a throw as `false` and to compose from `explain` when the method is absent; this fork (and `searchAll` before it) fails the row on a throw and lets the middleware's own refusal stand when absent. Both stricter, both uniform across held/unknown ids. Should-fix, docs: either the fork's docblock cites `searchAll` as the precedent it follows (it does) and the contract's note is widened to admit "fail the read" as a fail-closed reading, or nothing; no code change needed here.
- **Docs drift** (comment 6559948159): `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` names `canReadObject`'s callers (the elevation reads); the new caller is classified `not-a-door` in the core pin (`row-serving-door-exposure.pin.test.ts`), which is right — it chooses an arm, serves no row, and its `true` still reads through the middleware. The page is prose face: the seat's ACCEPT names whether a sentence is owed.
- **Fork comment accuracy**: the ⚠️ paragraph's first reason names the `403`/`404`-beside-`201` signal; it does not name the third outcome of the old fork (the landing in ① 4). Should-fix, one clause.
- `Clause-②: no` declared without the `(narrowing)` arm — judged right in ②; no `open_questions` block in the body; the body's "Changed" and "Unchanged" bullets hold against the diff.

### ④ Design judgment

No face asks it; recorded as the ruling-asked judgment of the fork against the text it implements. Ruling 5985885287 A: "a row the caller cannot read answers exactly what a nonexistent id answers" — on the upsert door a nonexistent id answers a create, and a create naming a held id has only the collision to give; the 2026-11-01 amendment states that reconciliation ("a create naming a held id has no 'nonexistent' answer to give, because the key it names is taken") and binds the answer to be the create's, with no detail of its own. The fork meets it: same `engine.insert`, same row builder, no new code, field or sentence; hidden-in-own-organization and other-organization rows answer alike (dogfood both suites). Ruling 5934879010 rule 2 is followed for the collision's code. The reversal of #5099/#5187 is recorded in the fork comment with the right citations and keeps #5099's no-fallback half. Holds.

Reviewed-by: `session_017xRBcVy4VXmkQjn2MGeaWk`

**VERDICT: PASS**

Must-fixes: none. Should-fixes: (1) PR body "Acceptance notes" — replace "was never written by this door" with the ① 4 reading (the arm is now unreachable for the edit-without-read class; before this diff that class could land where no write-class row filter bound); (2) pin the ① 4 class in the dogfood `HIDDEN` table (±create); (3) the planned docs-only PR adds the batch `upsert` by-id door to ADR-0120's amendment list, with the persisted driver-memory residual; (4) one clause in the fork comment naming the old fork's third outcome.
